title: Kubernetes node readiness comes from the Ready condition status
claim: Every K3s provider projection of Kubernetes node readiness derives ready and status from the node condition whose type is Ready and whose status is True. get-cluster-info and list-clusters use the same parser, preserve each node's ready/status fields, and derive aggregate counts from those node observations. A node condition type alone never means the node is Ready. The plugin catalog, installer descriptor, MCP server metadata, and HTTP discovery metadata report one identical provider version.
rationale: Projecting .status.conditions[-1].type labels a stopped node Ready because the condition type remains Ready while its status changes to False. That false state can make HA evidence and operator decisions untrustworthy.
owner: wunderous/host-agents owns the provider-neutral Kubernetes capability projection and the K3s provider implementation.

included: K3s provider get-cluster-info node status and aggregate readiness
K3s provider list-clusters node status and aggregate readiness
native Kubernetes Node condition and node-role metadata projection
excluded: Pod readiness, application data-plane health, or endpoint failover
node health interpretations owned by other Kubernetes providers

exception: Malformed Kubernetes node JSON or an unnamed node must fail the projection. A provider may not infer node readiness from node existence, condition ordering, instance status, or condition type. A different readiness definition requires an explicit superseding decision and consumer migration.

required: a focused regression projects a node with Ready=True as Ready and Ready=false as NotReady
get-cluster-info reports nodeCount and readyNodeCount from those parsed observations
list-clusters uses the same node parser and does not project condition type as status
the provider manifest, plugin catalog, install recipe, MCP server metadata, and HTTP discovery metadata report one matching provider version
the Host Agent release tag matches the npm package version and publishes the K3s artifact
the verifier checks source anchors and confirms the regression runs in the normal test target

revisionBehavior: Any change to the Ready condition interpretation, node status output, or aggregate readiness fields requires updating the focused test and reviewed whole-file anchors. Provider behavior increments the provider plugin version and install recipe together, and publishes the K3s artifact in the next Host Agent release tag before live claims use the revised projection. Every wire-facing provider version string must be derived from and match the same provider catalog version.
